what: Carlisle makes commercial roofing: the insulation, membranes and sealants that cover the flat roofs of warehouses, schools and offices, mostly in North America.
customers: Roofing contractors and distributors working on new commercial buildings and, increasingly, on re-roofing existing ones.
money: single-ply roofing membranes, insulation and accessories
sealants, waterproofing and building envelope products
moat: A distribution network and contractor loyalty built over decades: roofers are trained on a system and warranties tie the building owner to it for twenty years.
risks: Commercial construction starts fell with interest rates and have not fully recovered
Revenue has been flat around $5B for three years after the 2022 spike
Raw material costs, mostly oil-linked chemicals, move faster than list prices
opportunities: A 14.8% net margin and $750M of free cash flow on $5.2B of revenue, high for a building products company
Re-roofing is about three-quarters of the market and happens on a schedule rather than with the construction cycle
The company has been selling non-core businesses to concentrate on roofing, which earns the best margins
watch: Re-roofing volumes and whether price increases stick through the distribution channel.
